definition_provenance: The numbered user_definition fields preserve the supplied starting taxonomy. Simple explanations, evidence scopes, relationships, and limitations are authored drafts awaiting orthodontist review.
relationship_note: broader_ids and related_ids are educational navigation links, not diagnostic implications. Never automatically propagate present or absent labels through these links. Overlapping teeth can accompany crowding but do not automatically establish a measured space deficiency. Separate concepts may coexist.
scope_note: Evidence scopes describe the information needed to assess a concept, not validated model capabilities. A visible photographic finding means only an appearance in adequate supplied views. Confirm bite closure before interpreting bite relationships. Standard photographs do not establish roots, bone, skeletal diagnosis, growth, treatment need, severity, or physical measurements. Clinical-record concepts require appropriate history and examination; a clinician decides whether imaging is indicated. No trained classifier, orthodontist review, or accuracy is established by this taxonomy.
overlap_note: Overjet concerns horizontal incisor overlap; overbite concerns vertical incisor overlap. Small amounts of both can be normal. Keep their annotations separate and do not infer measurements from uncalibrated images.

categories.name: Tooth alignment and spacing
categories.description: Describe tooth positions and visible spaces while keeping underlying causes unconfirmed.

categories.name: Bite abnormalities
categories.description: Describe possible relationships between opposing teeth with the bite position documented.

categories.name: Tooth eruption and development
categories.description: Combine visible appearances with dentition stage, history, examination, and other clinically indicated records.

categories.name: Complex conditions and treatment history
categories.description: Record specialist-confirmed context and historical changes separately from photographic appearances.

conditions.name: Dental crowding
conditions.user_definition: Insufficient space for teeth to align properly.
conditions.simple_explanation: Some teeth may look packed together or sit outside a smooth row.
limitations: Visible overlap does not quantify available space.
Photo appearance does not determine treatment need.

conditions.name: Overlapping teeth
conditions.user_definition: Teeth overlap one another; usually a feature of crowding.
conditions.simple_explanation: One tooth appears to partly cover its neighbour when viewed along the arch.
limitations: Camera angle can create apparent overlap.
Overlap and crowding remain separate annotations.

conditions.name: Generalized spacing
conditions.user_definition: Gaps between several teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: Several spaces can be seen between neighbouring teeth.
limitations: Spaces do not establish developmental absence or another cause.
Dentition stage affects interpretation.

conditions.name: Midline diastema
conditions.user_definition: A gap between the central front teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: There is a space where the two middle front teeth would meet.
limitations: A gap can be developmental in mixed dentition.
An isolated gap is not generalized spacing.

conditions.name: Rotated teeth
conditions.user_definition: Teeth twisted around their long axis.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth appears turned compared with the line of neighbouring teeth.
limitations: Crown orientation does not show root position.
No rotation angle is inferred from the photograph.

conditions.name: Displaced teeth
conditions.user_definition: Teeth positioned outside their expected location in the dental arch.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth appears outside the usual row of teeth.
limitations: A position difference does not explain its cause.
Tooth identity must be established before assigning FDI numbers.

conditions.name: Buccally displaced teeth
conditions.user_definition: Teeth positioned too far toward the cheek.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth appears farther toward the cheek than the surrounding row.
limitations: An appropriate occlusal view is important for direction.
Visible position does not establish bone support.

conditions.name: Lingually or palatally displaced teeth
conditions.user_definition: Teeth positioned toward the tongue or roof of the mouth.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth appears farther toward the tongue or palate than the surrounding row.
limitations: Hidden surfaces may make the direction uncertain.
Displacement alone does not establish a crossbite.

conditions.name: Abnormally tipped teeth
conditions.user_definition: Teeth leaning abnormally toward neighbouring teeth or spaces.
conditions.simple_explanation: The visible crown appears to lean rather than stand in line with its neighbours.
limitations: Only apparent crown inclination can be described.
Root inclination and the amount of tipping need clinical records.

conditions.name: Proclined incisors
conditions.user_definition: Front teeth tilted outward.
conditions.simple_explanation: The front-tooth crowns appear tilted toward the lips.
limitations: Projection and tooth inclination are different observations.
No dental or skeletal classification follows automatically.

conditions.name: Retroclined incisors
conditions.user_definition: Front teeth tilted inward.
conditions.simple_explanation: The front-tooth crowns appear tilted toward the tongue or palate.
limitations: An apparent inward tilt alone does not establish Class II division 2.
Angle and root position are not measured here.

conditions.name: Dental midline discrepancy
conditions.user_definition: Upper and lower dental midlines do not align, or differ from the facial midline.
conditions.simple_explanation: The centres of the upper and lower front teeth appear offset.
limitations: Head tilt and camera perspective can mimic an offset.
A cropped mouth image cannot establish the facial midline.

conditions.name: Bimaxillary dental protrusion
conditions.user_definition: Upper and lower front teeth positioned excessively forward; requires clinical assessment.
conditions.simple_explanation: Both sets of front teeth may sit forward; a clinician must assess this relationship.
limitations: Intraoral photos alone do not establish dental protrusion relative to the face or jaw bases.
Forward inclination does not automatically imply excessive protrusion or a skeletal diagnosis.

conditions.name: Increased overjet
conditions.user_definition: Excessive horizontal distance between the upper and lower front teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: The upper front teeth appear farther ahead of the lower front teeth horizontally.
limitations: Bite closure and camera perspective must be documented.
An uncalibrated photograph cannot supply a millimetre measurement.

conditions.name: Reverse overjet / underbite appearance
conditions.user_definition: Lower front teeth sit ahead of the upper front teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: The lower front teeth appear ahead of the upper front teeth in the bite.
limitations: A reversed front-tooth relationship does not prove skeletal Class III.
A functional forward shift needs clinical assessment.

conditions.name: Deep overbite
conditions.user_definition: Upper front teeth cover an excessive amount of the lower front teeth vertically.
conditions.simple_explanation: The upper front teeth appear to cover much of the lower front teeth vertically.
limitations: Photographic overlap does not establish traumatic contact.
Overbite is vertical and must be recorded separately from overjet.

conditions.name: Traumatic deep bite
conditions.user_definition: A deep bite associated with injury to the gums or roof of the mouth.
conditions.simple_explanation: A deep bite is considered traumatic only when associated soft-tissue injury is clinically established.
limitations: Hidden gum or palatal contact cannot be excluded by photos.
A clinician must establish injury and its relationship to the bite.

conditions.name: Anterior open bite
conditions.user_definition: Front teeth lack normal vertical overlap when the back teeth bite together.
conditions.simple_explanation: A space remains between the front teeth while the back teeth are together.
limitations: An open mouth is not evidence of an open bite.
Posterior contact and the natural bite must be confirmed.

conditions.name: Posterior open bite
conditions.user_definition: Back teeth fail to contact when other teeth are in contact.
conditions.simple_explanation: Some back teeth appear separated even while other teeth touch.
limitations: A still image may not show actual contacts.
Erupting teeth and incomplete closure need to be distinguished clinically.

conditions.name: Anterior crossbite
conditions.user_definition: One or more upper front teeth bite behind the lower front teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: At least one upper front tooth appears behind its opposing lower tooth when biting.
limitations: A localized crossbite does not establish skeletal jaw discrepancy.
Clinical closure assessment is needed to identify a functional shift.

conditions.name: Unilateral posterior crossbite
conditions.user_definition: Upper back teeth bite inside the lower back teeth on one side.
conditions.simple_explanation: The upper back teeth appear inside the lower back teeth on one side.
limitations: Both sides are needed before calling the finding unilateral.
A functional sideways shift cannot be resolved from a still image.

conditions.name: Bilateral posterior crossbite
conditions.user_definition: Upper back teeth bite inside the lower back teeth on both sides.
conditions.simple_explanation: The upper back teeth appear inside the lower back teeth on both sides.
limitations: Both posterior regions must be visible in the natural bite.
This appearance does not establish a skeletal width problem.

conditions.name: Scissor bite
conditions.user_definition: Upper back teeth lie excessively outside the lower back teeth, preventing normal chewing contact.
conditions.simple_explanation: Upper back teeth pass outside the lower teeth instead of meeting their chewing surfaces normally.
limitations: Actual chewing contacts require clinical confirmation.
The finding does not identify the underlying jaw or tooth contribution.

conditions.name: Edge-to-edge bite
conditions.user_definition: Upper and lower front biting edges meet directly.
conditions.simple_explanation: The upper and lower front teeth appear to meet at their edges.
limitations: A posed forward bite can mimic edge-to-edge contact.
The observation does not establish a dental or skeletal classification.

conditions.name: Ectopic eruption
conditions.user_definition: A tooth erupts along an abnormal path or in an abnormal position.
conditions.simple_explanation: A developing tooth may be coming through away from its usual path or position.
limitations: Visible displacement does not by itself establish an eruption disorder.
Developmental history and clinical records are needed.

conditions.name: Impacted tooth
conditions.user_definition: A tooth fails to erupt because its eruption is obstructed or abnormal.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth that has not come through may be blocked or developing abnormally; records are needed.
limitations: An unseen tooth is not automatically impacted.
Localization requires examination and any imaging a clinician considers indicated.

conditions.name: Delayed eruption
conditions.user_definition: Tooth eruption occurs later than expected for the developmental stage.
conditions.simple_explanation: A clinician considers whether a tooth is taking longer to come through for this person's development.
limitations: Age, dentition stage, and eruption history are needed.
Absence in one photo cannot establish delay.

conditions.name: Asymmetric eruption
conditions.user_definition: Corresponding teeth on opposite sides erupt at substantially different times.
conditions.simple_explanation: Matching teeth on the two sides may be coming through at different times.
limitations: A single photograph cannot establish when each tooth erupted.
Records and developmental stage are needed before interpreting the difference.

conditions.name: Retained primary tooth
conditions.user_definition: A baby tooth remains beyond its expected replacement period.
conditions.simple_explanation: A baby tooth is still present when a clinician would expect its replacement to be assessed.
limitations: Small crown size alone does not reliably identify a primary tooth.
Age, tooth identity, and successor records are needed.

conditions.name: Infraocclusion / submerged tooth
conditions.user_definition: A tooth’s biting surface sits below neighbouring biting surfaces.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth appears lower than the nearby chewing surfaces.
limitations: Clinical context must distinguish relative submergence from a tooth still erupting.
Appearance alone does not diagnose ankylosis.

conditions.name: Supraeruption / overeruption
conditions.user_definition: A tooth extends beyond the expected biting plane.
conditions.simple_explanation: A tooth appears to extend farther into the bite than neighbouring teeth.
limitations: Perspective and uneven crown heights can mislead.
The biting plane and opposing contacts require clinical assessment.

conditions.name: Hypodontia
conditions.user_definition: Developmental absence of one to five permanent teeth, excluding wisdom teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: Some permanent teeth did not develop; this cannot be established by a gap alone.
limitations: Records must distinguish developmental absence from extraction, impaction, and delayed eruption.
The supplied tooth-count convention requires orthodontist review; do not count absent photo detections.

conditions.name: Oligodontia
conditions.user_definition: Developmental absence of six or more permanent teeth, excluding wisdom teeth.
conditions.simple_explanation: Several permanent teeth did not develop; a clinician needs to verify which teeth are absent.
limitations: A photographic tooth count does not establish developmental absence.
Review the tooth-count convention and developmental records with an orthodontist.

conditions.name: Supernumerary teeth / hyperdontia
conditions.user_definition: Extra teeth beyond the normal number.
conditions.simple_explanation: Additional teeth may be present, including teeth not yet visible in the mouth.
limitations: Primary and permanent teeth must be charted separately.
Photographs cannot exclude unerupted additional teeth.

conditions.name: Tooth transposition
conditions.user_definition: Two teeth develop or erupt in exchanged positions.
conditions.simple_explanation: Two teeth may appear to have exchanged their usual places.
limitations: Reliable tooth identity and developmental records are required.
Visible crown order does not establish the arrangement of the roots.

conditions.name: Transverse arch discrepancy
conditions.user_definition: Upper and lower dental arch widths do not coordinate properly.
conditions.simple_explanation: The widths of the upper and lower rows of teeth may not match in the bite.
limitations: Separately photographed arches cannot be compared as calibrated physical widths.
Tooth inclination and skeletal width need to be distinguished.

conditions.name: Jaw asymmetry
conditions.user_definition: Differences between the right and left sides of the jaws.
conditions.simple_explanation: The two sides of the jaws may differ; a specialist assesses the actual cause and significance.
limitations: Mouth-only photos do not establish jaw-bone asymmetry.
Head posture, perspective, and functional shifts need assessment.

conditions.name: Skeletal jaw discrepancy
conditions.user_definition: Abnormal relationships between the jaw bones; requires specialist assessment.
conditions.simple_explanation: A specialist assesses whether the jaw bones have a relationship that contributes to the bite.
limitations: Dental classification and tooth position do not establish a skeletal diagnosis.
Requires specialist examination and appropriate records; never infer from a photograph alone.

conditions.name: Cleft-associated malocclusion
conditions.user_definition: Bite abnormalities associated with cleft lip or palate.
conditions.simple_explanation: A person with a documented cleft may have bite findings needing specialist interpretation.
limitations: Requires a documented clinical history, not an inferred facial diagnosis.
Photographs do not establish the full cleft anatomy or previous care.

conditions.name: Other craniofacial anomaly-associated malocclusion
conditions.user_definition: Bite abnormalities associated with other developmental conditions affecting the face or skull.
conditions.simple_explanation: Some documented developmental conditions can affect the bite and need a specialist team's assessment.
limitations: Do not infer a syndrome or developmental diagnosis from appearance.
The associated condition must come from clinical records and specialist review.

conditions.name: Orthodontic relapse
conditions.user_definition: Teeth shift after previous orthodontic treatment; requires treatment history or earlier records.
conditions.simple_explanation: Teeth may have changed position after earlier orthodontic treatment.
limitations: A current photograph alone cannot establish a change over time.
Treatment history and comparable earlier records are required.

dental_classifications.name: Class I malocclusion
dental_classifications.definition: A clinician records Class I dental relationships using the applicable tooth landmarks; alignment or other bite findings may coexist.
dental_classifications.simple_explanation: The clinician's dental classification can be Class I even when some teeth are crowded or spaced.
limitations: Specify whether molar, canine, or incisor relationships are being recorded.
Class I is not proof of an ideal bite, no treatment need, or a particular skeletal relationship.

dental_classifications.name: Class II division 1
dental_classifications.definition: A clinician-entered Class II incisor classification with prominent upper incisors and increased overjet; posterior dental relationships are recorded separately.
dental_classifications.simple_explanation: This dental classification commonly describes upper front teeth projecting ahead of the lower front teeth.
limitations: Incisor appearance alone does not establish molar or canine classification.
This classification does not determine which jaw contributes or establish a skeletal diagnosis.

dental_classifications.name: Class II division 2
dental_classifications.definition: A clinician-entered Class II incisor classification with retroclined upper central incisors, often accompanied by increased overbite; posterior relationships are recorded separately.
dental_classifications.simple_explanation: The upper middle front teeth tilt inward in this clinical dental classification, often with greater vertical overlap.
limitations: A deep bite or an inward-tilted tooth alone does not establish this classification.
Do not infer the underlying skeletal relationship or a treatment plan.

dental_classifications.name: Class III malocclusion
dental_classifications.definition: A clinician records Class III dental relationships using specified incisor, canine, or molar landmarks; skeletal and functional assessments remain separate.
dental_classifications.simple_explanation: The clinician records a forward lower-dental relationship relative to the upper teeth using defined landmarks.
limitations: Reverse overjet does not automatically establish all Class III dental relationships.
Dental, functional, and skeletal contributions require separate assessment.

classification_note: These four classifications are clinician-entered records, separate from the 41 screening concepts. Record molar, canine, and incisor relationships independently where appropriate, including side and the classification system used. Never infer a skeletal class from a dental class.
